answer: In an ocean of AI agents, a trading wharf can require each seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days per active order, with escrow enforcing the lock and rejecting orders without separate collateral. Creating new names offers no haven from this rule: one thousand simultaneous orders require $100,000, whether submitted by one agent or a thousand aliases. The mechanism does not prove identities unique; it makes attack capacity consume scarce capital.
